title: Application of antiferroelectric like materials in non-volatile memory devices (US 10,056,393)
supports: Built-in bias from ~1 eV electrode work-function difference or stored charge makes AFE-like (PHL) films bistable; ZrO2 PHL films have higher endurance than doped HfO2; stronger AFE character gives better endurance (via search snippet) [B1-01]

title: Hafnia-based antiferroelectric tunnel junction (KAIST repository record)
supports: Two stable nonvolatile states from AFE films with asymmetric work-function electrodes and fixed oxide charge; AFTJ endurance >1e9 cycles and switching <30 ns (via search snippet) [B1-01]

title: SKKU repository record (Hf0.3Zr0.7O2 built-in-bias AFE)
supports: A Korean group reports Hf0.3Zr0.7O2 with built-in bias: nonvolatile symmetric half-loop at 1.25 V, endurance to 1e10 cycles (via search snippet; attribution to this record vs the KAIST record not pinned) [B1-01]

title: Negative-capacitance charge boosting in sub-10 nm TiN/Hf0.5Zr0.5O2/TiN DRAM cell capacitor (M. Kang, Y. Kang, J. Byun, S.E. Ahn)
supports: Ferroelectric NC proposed to increase DRAM cell stored charge; charge boosting analysed in sub-10 nm TiN/HZO/TiN DRAM capacitor (via search snippet) [B1-02]

title: Materials Futures (Jan 2024): stabilized negative capacitance in epitaxial HZO/Al2O3 and ZrO2/Al2O3 capacitors
supports: Capacitance enhancement of HZO/Al2O3 and ZrO2/Al2O3 bilayers vs isolated Al2O3 capacitor, cited as stabilized NC (epitaxial films) (via search snippet) [B1-02]

title: KU Leuven paper on ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 DRAM capacitor stacks
supports: Standard DRAM capacitor is a ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 stack; Al2O3 interlayer improves leakage but lowers effective k (via search snippet) [B1-01, B1-02]

title: 2T1D Memory Cell with Voltage Gain (W.K. Luk, R.H. Dennard, VLSI Symposium 2004)
supports: Gated diode acts as a non-linear capacitance that amplifies the stored voltage on read: higher S/N and low-voltage operation (via search snippet) [B1-03]

title: Gated diode memory cells (US 8,675,403)
supports: Gated diode stores charge only above threshold; cell gain ~4 with gated diode vs ~1 with linear capacitor at VS=1.2 V, VL_HIGH=0.4 V (via search snippet) [B1-03]

title: Suzhou Oriental Semiconductor (Wikipedia), citing Wang et al., Science 341:640 (2013)
supports: Semi-floating-gate transistor (Fudan, Science 2013): ~ns write at <2 V; floating gate tied to drain via embedded p-n diode/TFET (via search snippet) [B1-06]

title: Electronics 8(4):414 (MDPI) on semi-floating-gate capacitor-less memory
supports: SFG transistor proposed as capacitor-less DRAM; ~5 ns at <=2.0 V in simulation; embedded diode/TFET enlarges footprint and limits density (via search snippet; attribution to this record probable, not pinned) [B1-06]

title: US10256351B2 Semi-floating gate FET
supports: Semi-floating gate FET patent family (title-level, via search result) [B1-06]

title: Compact SRAM cell using tunnel diodes (US 6,342,718)
supports: Cites van der Wagt et al., 'RTD/HFET Low Standby Power SRAM Gain Cell', IEEE EDL vol.19 no.1: two tunnel diodes + one FET, ~50 nW per cell standby; GaAs expensive, nW/cell still too high (via search snippet) [B1-07]

title: ISDRS 2011 abstract on low-standby tunnel-diode SRAM
supports: Van der Wagt concept refined using diode junction capacitance to lower peak/valley current density; nA operation with InP/InGaAs RTDs; cites van der Wagt Proc. IEEE 87:571 (1999) (via search snippet) [B1-07]

title: Analysis of the use of molecular resonant tunneling diodes for local refresh of DRAM cells
supports: Prior proposal of in-cell NDR (molecular RTD) local refresh of DRAM cells (title-level, via search result) [B1-07]

title: Developing fatigue-resistant ferroelectrics using interlayer sliding switching (CAS news on Bian et al., Science 2024)
supports: Bilayer 3R-MoS2 sliding ferroelectric: no wake-up and no substantial fatigue after 1e6 cycles at 1-100 ms pulses; total field stress up to 1e5 s; immobile S-vacancy defects (via search snippet) [B1-12]

title: Sliding ferroelectrics offer fast, fatigue-free switching
supports: Bilayer boron nitride sliding-ferroelectric FET with endurance >1e11 cycles and ns-scale switching; fatigue-free described as intrinsic to sliding ferroelectricity (via search snippet; lab attribution in snippet uncertain) [B1-12]

title: Ultrafast high-endurance memory based on sliding ferroelectrics (NIMS dataset record)
supports: Dataset record titled 'Ultrafast high-endurance memory based on sliding ferroelectrics' (title-level, via search result) [B1-12]

title: Nonvolatile ferroelectric domain wall memory (Sharma et al., Science Advances 2017)
supports: Two-terminal domain-wall memory in LiNbO3: stored bit = presence of a conductive wall; nondestructive read <3 V, OFF/ON ~1e3, good endurance and retention (via search snippet) [B1-13]

title: High-Performance LiNbO3 Domain Wall Memory Devices with Enhanced Selectivity via Optimized Metal-Semiconductor Contact (Nanomaterials 2024)
supports: LiNbO3 domain-wall RAM with embedded selector, selectivity >1e6; aims at higher DW current density for fast low-voltage reads (via search snippet) [B1-13]

title: Giant and accessible conductivity of charged domain walls in lithium niobate
supports: Charged domain walls in LN can be highly conductive (title-level, via search result) [B1-13]

title: Nanosecond protonic programmable resistors for analog deep learning (Onen et al., Science 377:539, 2022)
supports: WO3 channel, nanoporous PSG proton electrolyte, Pd H reservoir; ~1 V/nm across PSG; nanosecond programming at room temperature; CMOS-native materials (via search snippet) [B1-16]

title: MIT protonic programmable resistor press release
supports: PSG electrolyte made the protonic resistor ~1e6x faster than the team's previous device; room temperature (press claim, via search snippet) [B1-16]

title: Molecular memory (Wikipedia)

title: Molecular memories (UC Riverside, Zaera group)

title: Molecular Memories, Once Doubted, Prove Durable and Practical

title: IEEE JXCDC (Jan 2022): shared SOT channel with multiple MTJs
publisher: IEEE J. Exploratory Solid-State Computational Devices and Circuits
supports: Sharing one SOT channel and write transistor among MTJs: more than four MTJs per channel faces IR-drop and write-error-rate limits (via search snippet) [B1-15]

title: Spin-Orbit-Torque-based Devices, Circuits and Architectures (review)
supports: Series MTJs on a shared (curved) SOT track with different switching currents allow selective writing (via search snippet) [B1-15]

title: Stacked spin-orbit-torque magnetoresistive random-access memory (US 11,251,362)
supports: Multiple SOT-MRAM cells on a common spin-Hall layer sharing driving transistors (via search snippet) [B1-15]

title: Nano-electro-mechanical DRAM cell (US 8,432,723)

title: Designing Low Power and Durable Digital Blocks Using Shadow Nano-Electromechanical Relays (IEEE TVLSI 2016)

title: Design of Almost-Nonvolatile Embedded DRAM Using Nanoelectromechanical Relay Devices (DATE 2020)

title: Sense amplifier circuit and semiconductor device (US 8,320,208)

title: High-speed charge transfer sense amplifier for 0.5 V DRAM array applications
